## Steps

<figure class="story-hero"><a href="/forge-studio/media/stories/S6/01-open-studio-on-the-knowledge-pillar.png"><img src="/forge-studio/media/stories/S6/01-open-studio-on-the-knowledge-pillar.png" alt="1. Open Studio on the Knowledge pillar"></a></figure>

1. **Open Studio on the Knowledge pillar.** Knowledge is where everything forge has learned lives, as graphs it can read back.
2. **Press "+ New KB".** One form, and the only two things that matter on it are what this knowledge base is called and what it is bound to.
3. **Name it, bind it to the forge-develop flow, scope it to the review-band, and create it.** Binding is the act.
4. **Follow the seeding session forge started for it.** Creating a knowledge base starts an agent that fills it.
5. **Brief the seeding agent on what this knowledge base is for, and let it read.** A band-scoped knowledge base has no project repo to read — it reads the Flow’s own archived cycles, and synthesises what review kept finding.
6. **Read the themes it drafted and approve them into the knowledge base.** Nothing an agent drafts enters the brain without a human saying yes.
7. **Back on the knowledge base, find a real theme in the graph.** Seeded means there is something in it.
8. **Go to the Projects pillar to find the project on the other end of that binding.** A knowledge base is bound to a Flow, and a Flow runs against projects.
9. **Open story-s6.** story-s6 is provisioned from the node-library fixture for this run, so it is the project a clean checkout can plan against.
10. **Press "Architect →" to plan a piece of work on it.** A knowledge base earns its keep at planning time.
11. **Describe the work, cap what this run may spend, and press "Start architect".** The planner is a real agent and a real agent costs money, so the operator caps this run before starting it.
12. **Open the architect session it just started.** What happens next is the thing S6 exists to prove.
13. **Go back to the knowledge base and see that the planner actually read it — the brain-index event, naming this KB and what it took.** This is the beat the whole product rests on.
14. **Open the knowledge base’s Health tab and drain it to green.** A seeded knowledge base is not a healthy one.
15. **Read the diff the drain proposes, file by file, before accepting it.** This is where S6 ends: a rendered diff, per file, of what an agent changed inside the operator’s knowledge — not a claim that it cleared N findings.
